findings.title: Unrestricted Local File Inclusion via Include Directive
findings.description: The `Include` directive in `src/mistune/directives/include.py` resolves user-provided paths relative to the source directory. While there is a basic path check, it fails to account for symbolic links or OS-specific path normalization vulnerabilities, potentially allowing attackers to read sensitive files on the server filesystem.
steps_to_exploit: Construct a malicious Markdown file containing the `.. include::` directive.
Target a sensitive file path outside the intended directory, such as `/etc/passwd` or application config files.
Trigger the parser on the malicious file.
View the injected file content in the rendered HTML output.
findings.impact: Full read access to arbitrary files on the host machine, potentially leading to credential theft or system compromise.

findings.title: Potential Arbitrary Code Execution in `serve-doc.py`
findings.description: The `serve-doc.py` file uses `livereload.shell` to execute a command string directly from the filesystem. If an attacker can influence the `make build-docs` command or the environment in which it runs, they could execute arbitrary shell commands.
steps_to_exploit: Modify the Makefile or create a malicious binary named 'make' in a directory accessible to the path.
Execute `serve-doc.py` which triggers the `shell` command.
Arbitrary code is executed with the privileges of the script runner.
findings.impact: Arbitrary command execution on the host machine.

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsafe URL Handling
findings.description: In `src/mistune/renderers/html.py`, the `safe_url` method allows 'javascript:' or other dangerous protocols if the `allow_harmful_protocols` flag is set to true by the user or if the protocol isn't correctly identified as safe.
steps_to_exploit: Create a markdown link or image tag with a URI like `javascript:alert(1)`.
Configure the library (or rely on misconfiguration) to allow harmful protocols.
The malicious URI is rendered into an `href` or `src` attribute without sufficient sanitization.
findings.impact: XSS in the context of the user's browser, enabling session hijacking or unauthorized actions.

findings.title: Insecure `open()` in Command Line Tool
findings.description: The `_output` function in `src/mistune/__main__.py` uses `open(args.output, "w")` to write the output file without validating the path. This can be exploited to overwrite sensitive system files if the user runs the tool with elevated privileges.
steps_to_exploit: Run the CLI tool as a user with write permissions to sensitive directories.
Provide a path to a sensitive file (e.g., `/etc/cron.d/malicious`) via the `-o` flag.
The tool overwrites the target file with the rendered output.
findings.impact: System-wide file corruption or privilege escalation through file overwrite.

findings.title: ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) in Inline Parsing
findings.description: The inline parsing regexes, specifically those for complex structures, are prone to catastrophic backtracking when provided with deeply nested or crafted input strings.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a large input string containing repeated ambiguous markers that trigger regex backtracking.
Supply this input to the `markdown()` function.
The parser consumes excessive CPU resources.
findings.impact: Application denial of service due to CPU exhaustion.

findings.title: Insecure Default Configuration for HTML Rendering
findings.description: The library defaults `escape=true`, but the provided code snippet `html: Markdown = create_markdown(escape=false, ...)` suggests that common usage patterns or provided presets may disable HTML escaping by default, increasing XSS risks.
steps_to_exploit: User imports the provided `html` object directly.
User parses untrusted markdown input.
HTML tags within the markdown are rendered without sanitization.
findings.impact: Widespread XSS vulnerability in applications using the default library instance.

findings.title: Information Leakage via Unvalidated Directive Content
findings.description: The `Admonition` and `Image` directives allow passing attributes and content which might include sensitive metadata from the environment if the parser is improperly configured.
steps_to_exploit: Supply input markdown that includes directive options which are rendered into HTML attributes.
Expose potentially sensitive information about the file structure or environment through these attributes.
findings.impact: Exposure of sensitive environment/system configuration data.

findings.title: Circular Reference in `Include` Directive
findings.description: While the code attempts to check for circular references, the `include_stack` management is complex and prone to edge cases where deep recursion might bypass the check, potentially causing stack overflow or high memory usage.
steps_to_exploit: Create two files that include each other.
Trigger the parser on these files.
The recursive include might bypass simple stack depth limits in certain environments.
findings.impact: Denial of service via stack overflow.

findings.title: Insecure Input Handling in `read_stdin`
findings.description: Reading from `stdin` without enforcing size limits allows attackers to pipe massive amounts of data into the parser, potentially leading to memory exhaustion (OOM).
steps_to_exploit: Pipe a multi-gigabyte file into the standard input of the application.
The application reads the full input into memory for parsing.
findings.impact: Denial of service via OOM (Out Of Memory).

findings.title: Bypass of `_is_safe_url` via multiple decoding
findings.description: The `_unquote_url` function applies `unquote` three times. An attacker can craft a nested encoded URL that bypasses the `safe_url` check because the final, decoded protocol string (e.g., `java script:`) might be blocked, but the intermediate one might not, or vice versa.
steps_to_exploit: Encode a malicious URL three times in a specific way.
The `safe_url` function checks the partially decoded URL, which appears safe.
The browser decodes the URL one final time to the malicious protocol.

findings.title: Insecure Method Assignment for `process_text`
findings.description: The `abbr` plugin replaces a core method `process_text` using `types.MethodType`. This modifies the instance globally for that parser object and may introduce unexpected behavior or race conditions if the parser instance is shared across threads.
steps_to_exploit: Use a shared `Markdown` instance across multiple threads.
Install the `abbr` plugin which dynamically alters the behavior of the shared parser.
This leads to incorrect processing of text tokens in parallel operations.
findings.impact: Non-deterministic parsing errors or potential logical exploits.

findings.title: Improper escaping in `render_html_include`
findings.description: The `Include` directive renders HTML content within a `<pre>` tag. If the encoding of the included file is manipulated or handled incorrectly, content could break out of the tag.
steps_to_exploit: Include a file with a non-standard encoding that, when interpreted as UTF-8, results in HTML injection markers.
The result is rendered into the `pre` tag.

findings.title: Use of Assertions for Logic Flow
findings.description: Many parts of the code use `assert` for validation (e.g., checking if text is not null). In Python, if the code is run with optimization flags (`python -O`), these assertions are removed, potentially leading to null pointer exceptions or logic failures.
steps_to_exploit: Run the application with the `-O` or `-OO` Python flag.
Provide an input that causes the parser to hit a state the assertion was meant to catch.
The application continues execution in an undefined or invalid state.

findings.title: Sensitive Information in `_cached_parsers`
findings.description: The global `__cached_parsers` dictionary in `src/mistune/__init__.py` caches fully initialized `Markdown` instances. These instances contain the internal state of previous parses, which may include sensitive data from the parsed text.
steps_to_exploit: An attacker forces the application to parse a file containing sensitive information.
The parser, which holds this data in its `env` or other structures, is cached.
A subsequent, separate parsing request might access or leak data if the parser is reused with shared states.
findings.impact: Sensitive data leak across separate parsing operations.

findings.title: Insecure Temporary Files in `Makefile`
findings.description: The `Makefile` uses `rm -fr` on directories like `build/` and `dist/`. If these directories were created with weak permissions or exist in a shared environment, it could lead to race conditions or file deletion attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Create a symlink in the `build/` directory pointing to a sensitive location.
Wait for the developer or a CI process to run `make clean`.
The `rm -fr` command follows the symlink and deletes the target.
findings.impact: Arbitrary file deletion with the privileges of the user running `make`.
